instruction: more_itertools.one() and only() accept custom exceptions through too_short= and too_long=. If the supplied exception instance is falsy (for example an Exception subclass whose __bool__ returns False), it is ignored and the default ValueError is raised instead. Always raise the caller's exception whenever one was supplied. Also, when too_long is supplied, do not build the default error message at all: building it calls repr() on items of the iterable, and that repr may itself raise and hide the requested exception. Add tests.
instruction_source: written from the fix commit message, linked issue and hidden tests; describes behavior, not the change
